posts.title: Why use a Password Manager
posts.excerpt: Repeating passwords across websites for your email login is one of the easiest ways to let a fraudist cause you trouble
content: One of the most effortless ways to hack into a targets account is by counting on password re-use. Every year many popular websites like zomato,linkedin,dominoes are hacked and the exploit database is dumped publicly . Often these include compromising information such as geolocation at best and government IDs at worst . Why is this so bad? Because it unlocks the room for fraudists to log into your unrelated accounts such as say crypto exchange,gmail,socials etc by re-using the dumped password and hoping you re-use it everywhere.The way it can get real bad is by social engineering techniques notably sim swapping wherein the attacker hijacks your phone number and sim through talking nicely with the customer service representative . These techniques are elevated by seemingly non usefull information such as geolocation helping with deciding on proxies and mule networks and government IDs with sim swapping. If this sounds worrying you can lookup your or some important persons email on websites like haveibeenpwned.com you will be surprised by how many are a positive. This is mostly a problem with websites who dont hash or use obsolete hashing algos like md5.
